name: Cameroon
summary: Six ecological zones in nine hundred kilometres: an active 4,095 m volcano, Atlantic black sand, Korup rainforest, the Grassfields kingdoms and the Sahel edge at Waza.
window_alt: Black volcanic sand and palms below a volcano at dusk
when: Dry from November to February in the south; the north stays dry into April.

entries.caption: Africa in Miniature
entries.description: Volcano, rainforest, highlands, coast and Sahel — one country, six climates, fourteen days on the road.
entries.subject: the upper slopes of Mount Cameroon at dawn above the Atlantic

entries.caption: Six Climates, One Country
entries.description: The Cameroon Volcanic Line runs from the Gulf of Guinea to the Mandara mountains, changing the landscape every two hours of driving.
entries.subject: layered green highland ridges in the Bamenda highlands

entries.caption: Wildlife of the Rainforest
entries.description: Forest elephants, drills and chimpanzees in Korup and Dja — one of the oldest and least disturbed rainforests in Africa.
entries.subject: forest elephants among buttressed trees in Korup National Park

entries.caption: Sahel Safari at Waza
entries.description: Flat acacia savanna in the Far North, where elephant, giraffe and antelope gather at the last dry-season waterholes.
entries.subject: elephants and giraffe at a dry-season waterhole in Waza National Park

entries.caption: The 4,095 m Volcano
entries.description: Mount Cameroon is the highest point in West Africa and still active — three days up through farm, forest, grass and bare cinder.
entries.subject: trekkers on the open upper slopes of Mount Cameroon above the tree line

entries.caption: Where the River Meets the Sea
entries.description: The Lobé falls near Kribi drop straight over black rock into the Atlantic — one of very few waterfalls on earth that do.
entries.subject: the Lobe waterfalls pouring over rock directly into the Atlantic near Kribi

entries.caption: The Benoue and the Crater Lakes
entries.description: Gallery forest along the Bénoué in the north, and the volcanic crater lakes of Barombi Mbo and Nyos in the west.
entries.subject: the wide brown Benoue river with gallery forest along the bank

entries.caption: Black Sand and Warm Water
entries.description: Volcanic grey-black sand at Limbe, white sand and fishing pirogues at Kribi, warm all year on both.
entries.subject: surf breaking on volcanic black sand at dusk on the Cameroon coast near Limbe

entries.caption: Inside Korup
entries.description: One of the oldest rainforests in Africa, with a canopy suspension bridge over the Mana river and 400 tree species.
entries.subject: a canopy suspension bridge over a river inside Korup rainforest

entries.caption: Summit, Crater, Coast
entries.description: The Guinness route to 4,095 m, down the north flank to Mann's Spring, and out to the sea on the same trip.
entries.subject: walkers crossing grass slopes below the summit huts on Mount Cameroon

entries.caption: The Grassfields Kingdoms
entries.description: Bamileke and Bamoun chiefdoms in the west, still functioning, with palaces, secret societies and their own calendars.
entries.subject: a carved and beaded royal throne inside a palace museum at Foumban

entries.caption: Fulani, Mafa and Bamileke
entries.description: Two hundred and fifty ethnic groups and as many languages, from the Mafa terraces of the Mandara to the Fulani of the Sahel.
entries.subject: a Mafa farmer on the terraced slopes of the Mandara mountains

entries.caption: Ndole, Poulet DG and Grilled Fish
entries.description: Bitterleaf and groundnut ndolé, plantain, and whole fish grilled on the sand at Kribi within sight of the boat.
entries.subject: grilled fish and plantain served at a beachside stall in Kribi

entries.caption: Nguon at Foumban
entries.description: The Bamoun Nguon, a thousand years old and UNESCO-listed, where the sultan answers to his people before the dancing starts.
entries.subject: masked dancers and horsemen at the Nguon festival in Foumban

entries.caption: The Foumban Bronze Casters
entries.description: Lost-wax bronze, beaded thrones and carved masks made on the craft street the same way they were three centuries ago.
entries.subject: a bronze caster working molten metal in a workshop at Foumban

entries.caption: The Sultan's Palace
entries.description: The 1917 palace at Foumban and its museum of the Bamoun kings, plus the German colonial buildings still standing in Buea.
entries.subject: the Sultan's Palace at Foumban with its museum of the Bamoun kings

entries.caption: Dja, Rhumsiki and the Mandara
entries.description: The Dja Faunal Reserve is UNESCO World Heritage; the volcanic spires above Rhumsiki are the image on the old banknote.
entries.subject: volcanic rock spires rising from farmland at Rhumsiki in the Mandara mountains

entries.caption: Douala and Yaounde
entries.description: The port that moves the country and the hill capital that governs it, ninety minutes apart by air and nothing alike.
entries.subject: a street in the Bonapriso quarter of Douala

entries.caption: Chefferie and Colonial Buea
entries.description: Bamileke chefferie compounds with carved posts and conical roofs, and the German Schloss on the hill above Buea.
entries.subject: a Bamileke chieftaincy compound with carved posts and a conical thatched roof

entries.caption: Marche Central, Motos, Rain
entries.description: Bilingual, loud and unbothered: Douala's markets, the moto-taxis, and the sudden rain everyone waits out under an awning.
entries.subject: traders and moto-taxis in a busy Douala market street

entries.caption: Village and Mountain Together
entries.description: Guides and porters come from the mountain villages in rotation, and the trail money goes back into the village fund.
entries.subject: villagers and guides repairing a stone section of mountain trail together

entries.caption: The Ring Road on Foot
entries.description: Crater lakes, tea slopes and the Ring Road through the Bamenda highlands, walkable in sections between 1,200 and 2,000 m.
entries.subject: open dry-season slopes and ridge lines on Mount Cameroon

entries.caption: Kribi, Slowly
entries.description: Small beach hotels south of Kribi, a driver who knows the road, and nothing at all scheduled after lunch.
entries.subject: a small beach hotel terrace above the sand at Kribi

entries.caption: Korup, Dja and the Village Fund
entries.description: Ecotourism permits in Korup and Dja are issued through the villages, and the mountain trek runs on the Mount CEO rotation.
entries.subject: a forest guide identifying a tree species inside Korup rainforest

entries.caption: Cloud on the Rainforest
entries.description: Wet season cloud sitting on the forest above Buea, and dry season light on the Mandara spires — two countries, one lens.
entries.subject: cloud and rain sitting on the rainforest above Buea

entries.caption: The 1999 Lava Fields
entries.description: Black lava tongues from the 1999 and 2000 flows running down to the sea near Bakingili, with green already coming back.
entries.subject: black solidified lava flows reaching the sea on the flank of Mount Cameroon

entries.caption: Everything, Within One Border
entries.description: Sea level to Sahel in nine hundred kilometres, French and English on the same road, and almost nobody else on it.
entries.subject: a 4x4 on a red laterite road between rainforest and highland farmland

$calls: All eight, and the only country in the set that claims all eight. Its tagline is not decoration: Africa in miniature is what Cameroon is called because desert, Sahel, rainforest, savanna, highlands and coast are all inside one border. The list used to omit wildlife and food while the country file carried Waza's elephant and giraffe, Korup and Dja's forest elephants and drills, and ndole and Poulet DG written up in full — under-claiming against its own pages.
